newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Refugees still in Bangladesh as deadline passes.
newsitem.headline: Refugees still in Bangladesh as deadline passes.

text.p: A deadline for repatriating Moslem refugees from Burma passed with more than 22,000 still stranded in Bangladesh, officials said on Wednesday.
"Over 22,000 Rohingya refugees are still in three camps and no one knows when they will go home," one official told Reuters in Chittagong.

In January Dhaka and Rangoon set a deadline of March 31 to complete the repatriation of more than 250,000 refugees, who fled to Bangladesh in early 1992 from west Burma's Arakan state to escape what they said was military persecution.
Bangladeshi officials said on Wednesday the deadline was missed because Burmese immigration officials delayed giving clearance for all those waiting to return home.
"The repatriation process had been stopped as of April 1," one official said.
Repatriation began in September 1992 following an agreement between the two governments.
The number of returnees totalled 236,819 up to March 31 while 22,058 are still waiting, according to official figures.
However, A.K.M. Kamrul Huda, Bangladesh's Refugee Repatriation Commissioner, said he expected the process to resume soon.
"We are trying to have talks with the Burmese authorities to be able to send the remaining Rohingyas to their homeland in the near future," he said on Tuesday night.
The repatriation has been supervised by the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees.
